title: AP-MT066-AcpContractTestsWindowsHardening

scope.summary:
GOAL: Contract-test the ACP lane against LIVE third-party ACP agents (claude-agent-acp at minimum; gemini and the codex adapter when installed) and harden the Windows-specific failure modes, so adapter drift, capability gaps, and version bumps surface as typed evidence instead of silent lane breakage. Deliverables: (1) a live contract-test suite covering initialize/capability negotiation, a real prompt turn, cancel, and session/load resume — INCLUDING a Windows path-encoding resume regression test (the claude adapter historically had a Windows path-encoding resume blocker; Handshake runs on Windows, so this is a first-class regression, not an edge case); (2) an ADAPTER-GAP LEDGER: expected-vs-observed capability matrix per agent where every miss is a typed known-gap row (e.g. claude-agent-acp missing usage/cost events), never silence; (3) VERSION-RANGE PIN per registry agent with capability feature-detection preferred over version comparison; (4) typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF settlement when a live agent is absent from the host — the suite must never fake a live PASS and never hard-fail the whole build because an external CLI is missing.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New test file src/backend/handshake_core/tests/acp_live_contract.rs + support module tests/acp_contract_support/ (gap-ledger writer, agent availability probe, resume-path fixtures). Product-code touch limited to the MT-064 registry: recording observed capability/version evidence and the version_range pin enforcement hook (agent_registry.rs only). Gap-ledger artifact written to the external artifacts root (Handshake_Artifacts), not the repo worktree.

DETAILED SPEC:
- AVAILABILITY PROBE: for each registry agent, resolve + identity-verify via MT-064. Unresolvable or unverifiable => every live test for that agent settles as a typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF outcome (recorded in the gap ledger with the probe failure), the suite still exits green with the blocker rows visible in output. Installed-but-tampered is NOT a blocker: identity verification failure is a hard typed FAIL (supply-chain signal).
- CONTRACT TESTS (per available agent, claude-agent-acp mandatory when installed):
  1. initialize: protocol version accepted; capability negotiation completes; observed capabilities recorded verbatim into the gap ledger; MT-061 capability mapping asserted (steer_mid_turn=false; resume mirrors observed loadSession).
  2. prompt turn: session/new in a temp worktree (path WITH spaces), send a trivial deterministic prompt, receive streamed agent_message_chunk updates and a terminal stop reason; TurnItem stream asserted non-empty and ordered; stop reason in the known set (or typed unknown row).
  3. cancel: start a long-running prompt, send session/cancel, assert the in-flight prompt settles with stop reason cancelled within the bounded deadline (protocol MUST); a violation is a typed contract-violation row + test failure for that agent.
  4. resume (capability-gated): create session, complete a turn, drop the connection/process, relaunch, session/load the same session id, assert history/context loads and a follow-up turn works. WINDOWS PATH-ENCODING REGRESSION: run the resume matrix over cwd variants — path with spaces, mixed-separator path, drive-letter casing variant, and a non-ASCII segment — the historical claude adapter blocker class; each variant is its own assertion row.
  5. client-services smoke: a prompt that induces a permission request and an fs read (agents differ in inducibility — when an agent cannot be deterministically induced, record the row as NOT_INDUCIBLE with reason instead of skipping silently).
- ADAPTER-GAP LEDGER (schema hsk.acp_adapter_gap_ledger@1): per agent: { agent_id, adapter_version_observed, probe_status, rows: [{ capability_or_behavior, expected (from MT-064 registry declaration), observed, status: OK | KNOWN_GAP | CONTRACT_VIOLATION | NOT_INDUCIBLE | NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF, reason }] }. Mandatory seeded expectations: claude-agent-acp usage/cost events => expected ABSENT (known gap July 2026) — if the adapter STARTS emitting usage events, the ledger flags the improvement as a row (status OK with 'gap closed' reason) so MT-065's D18 parity row can be upgraded; loadSession presence; permission-request flow presence.
- VERSION-RANGE PIN: each registry agent carries a tested version_range (MT-064 field). The contract suite records the observed adapter version; outside-range => typed VERSION_OUT_OF_RANGE row and the registry launch path emits a typed warning event (not a hard block by default — capability feature-detection is authoritative per the WP stub research; version pin is the tripwire, capabilities are the contract).
- NO PANIC HARDENING: all live-agent interaction runs under the MT-061 typed-error surface; a misbehaving agent (garbage JSON, early exit, never-ending stream) must settle typed within bounded deadlines — one chaos-ish test per failure class using the fixture agent in misbehave mode (garbage frame, mid-turn exit, cancel-ignore) to prove the harness itself cannot hang.

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Implement the availability probe over the MT-064 registry (resolve + verify, typed outcomes).
2. Implement the gap-ledger writer (schema above, serde, atomic write to external artifacts root).
3. Author contract tests 1-5 parameterized per agent; wire the NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF settlement path.
4. Author the Windows resume matrix (4 path variants) as separate named assertions.
5. Add the version-observation + VERSION_OUT_OF_RANGE tripwire into agent_registry.rs (minimal hook; feature-detection remains authoritative).
6. Author the fixture-agent misbehave-mode chaos tests (garbage frame, mid-turn exit, cancel-ignore) proving bounded typed settlement.
7. Run the full suite on the Windows host with claude-agent-acp installed; capture the gap ledger; verify green-with-typed-blockers behavior by also running with an agent deliberately absent from PATH.
forbidden_paths: .GOV/** (the bridge is READ-ONLY reference for parity; never edited by this WP)
src/frontend/** (no GUI surface in this MT)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/agent_sessions/acp/client_core.rs (behavior owned by MT-061; contract tests consume, do not patch)
acceptance_criteria: With claude-agent-acp installed and identity-verified, contract tests 1-4 pass live: initialize negotiation, real prompt turn with streamed updates and known stop reason, cancel settling cancelled within deadline, and capability-gated resume via session/load.

The Windows resume matrix runs all 4 path variants (spaces, mixed separators, drive-letter casing, non-ASCII segment) as separately named assertions; any failure reproduces the historical path-encoding blocker class as a typed CONTRACT_VIOLATION row, not a vague suite failure.

The adapter-gap ledger is written to the external artifacts root, parses against hsk.acp_adapter_gap_ledger@1, and contains the seeded claude-agent-acp expectation rows including usage/cost events expected-ABSENT; a missing capability is a typed KNOWN_GAP row, never a silent skip.

When a registry agent is absent from the host, its live tests settle as typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF rows and the suite exits green with the blockers visible — proven by running with an agent deliberately unresolvable; an installed-but-tampered agent is a hard typed FAIL instead.

Observed adapter version is recorded per agent; an out-of-range version yields a typed VERSION_OUT_OF_RANGE row and a typed registry warning event; capability feature-detection remains the authoritative gate (asserted: no test passes/fails on version compare alone).

Fixture-agent misbehave modes (garbage frame, mid-turn exit, cancel-ignore) each settle typed within bounded deadlines — the harness cannot hang (the >5-minute-hang failure class from prior WP validation history is explicitly guarded against).
Client-services smoke rows exist per agent with OK or NOT_INDUCIBLE-with-reason status; nothing silently skipped.
cargo build -p handshake_core green; suite passes headless; zero visible windows (HBR-QUIET-001); no repo-worktree artifact writes.
implementation_notes: LIVE-AGENT REALITY: this host is Windows and the operator uses claude-agent-acp-class tooling; the live claude leg is expected to actually run here. gemini/codex legs settle as typed blockers when not installed — that is the designed honest outcome, not a failure.

The Windows path-encoding resume blocker is a documented historical claude-adapter defect class (WP-017 stub risks_unknowns); even if fixed upstream, the regression matrix stays — it guards Handshake's own cwd/session-id handling too (MT-061 binds cwd; MT-063 scope guard normalizes the same paths).

Version pin philosophy (WP stub research): feature-detect capabilities at initialize instead of comparing versions; the version_range is a tripwire that makes drift visible, not a gate that blocks a working adapter.
Gap-ledger rows feed MT-065's parity report (D18 token-usage GAP_TYPED cites the claude usage-events row) — keep row ids stable so the parity report can reference them.
Deterministic prompts: use a fixed instruction with a fixed expected-shape reply check that tolerates model nondeterminism (assert structure/stop-reason, not exact text).

Live tests must bound EVERY await (initialize, turn, cancel, resume) with explicit deadlines and typed timeout settlement — the prior-WP validator history shows unbounded external-process waits are the most expensive failure mode in this repo.
npx-launched adapters may incur first-run download latency; the probe should pre-warm or use a generous first-launch deadline, recorded in output.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless backend MT: live protocol contract tests and typed gap ledgering; no operator-visible surface. TraceProjection/ledger reconstruction per HBR-VIS-004.

target_entries: Agent sessions: ACP adapter support status — tested agents, version ranges, known adapter gaps (where the gap ledger lives and how to read it)

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations: FLIGHT_RECORDER: contract-violation, known-gap, and version-out-of-range findings are business events — FR emit per MT-161 kinds when landed, else DEFERRED-with-reason.
INTERNAL_DIAGNOSTICS: expose per-agent probe status and last contract-run verdict to the open diagnostic-event API — WIRED or DEFERRED-with-reason.
PALMISTRY: live third-party agent runs are the highest freeze/hang risk in the ACP family — register live contract runs under the external watcher when available, else DEFERRED-with-reason.
risk_if_missed: Adapter drift lands silently: an adapter rename/version bump or a Windows path regression breaks the ACP lane in production with no typed evidence, the known usage-events gap stays undocumented (corrupting MT-065 parity claims), and misbehaving agents can hang governed sessions unboundedly.

risks: RISK-1: Fabricated live evidence — an absent agent whose tests report PASS (or are skipped invisibly) converts missing proof into false confidence (the exact class the typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF discipline exists to prevent).
RISK-2: Silent capability gaps — a missing adapter behavior that produces no ledger row (e.g. usage events) lets downstream parity/billing claims rest on nothing.
RISK-3: Unbounded live waits — a hung adapter turn or ignored cancel stalls the suite >5 minutes (repo-documented validator failure class) and, worse, would stall production sessions the same way.
RISK-4: Version-pin theater — gating on version strings while capabilities drift within a version (or pass across versions) gives false security in both directions.
RISK-5: Windows regression blind spot — testing only ASCII no-space paths misses the exact encoding class that already broke the claude adapter on Windows.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): availability probe with typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF settlement; deliberate-absence test proves the path; tampered-agent hard-fail keeps the blocker honest.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): expected-vs-observed matrix seeded from MT-064 registry declarations; every expectation MUST produce a row; ledger completeness asserted.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): every live await carries an explicit bounded deadline with typed timeout settlement; misbehave-mode chaos tests prove the harness settles.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): capability feature-detection is authoritative; version range is a tripwire row only; a test asserts no pass/fail decision rests on version compare alone.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): the 4-variant Windows path matrix (spaces, separators, drive casing, non-ASCII) is contract-pinned as separately named assertions.

research_provenance.source: agentclientprotocol.com (initialize/capability negotiation, session/load capability gating, cancel MUST-settle-cancelled semantics) + July-2026 adapter ecosystem facts from the WP-017 stub research basis (claude adapter renamed @zed-industries/claude-code-acp -> @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp; known gaps: no usage/cost events, historical Windows path-encoding resume blocker; Gemini CLI native ACP; Codex via Zed adapter) + repo precedent: WP-KERNEL-012 MT-045 validation history (unbounded external-process waits as the most expensive failure class) + MT-064 registry declarations as the expected-capability source.
corrections: Absent live agents produce typed blockers with a green suite — the repo's NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF convention — instead of red builds or fake passes.
Feature-detection over version comparison is the authoritative gate (WP stub research decision); the version pin is retained only as a drift tripwire.
The Windows resume matrix is kept permanently even if the upstream adapter bug is fixed, because it also covers Handshake's own path normalization surfaces (MT-061/MT-063).
